pages.title: GDP
pages.description: How fast the euro area economy is growing, what is driving it and how the big economies compare.

sections.title: Growth
sections.intro: Real GDP is the value of everything the euro area produces, adjusted for prices. Quarterly growth is noisy; the change on a year earlier is the steadier read.

sections.title: Across countries
sections.intro: The same growth rate, country by country, on one shared scale.

pages.title: Labour
pages.description: Jobs, unemployment and how hard it is for employers to find workers.

sections.title: Unemployment and vacancies
sections.intro: Unemployment is close to its lowest since the euro began. Vacancies tell you whether employers still want more people.

sections.title: Across countries
sections.intro: Unemployment by country, darker where it is higher.

pages.title: Wages
pages.description: What workers are being paid, and whether pay is keeping up with prices.

sections.title: Pay growth
sections.intro: Negotiated wages are the deals unions and employers sign. The ECB tracker reads the deals already signed for the year ahead.

pages.title: Inflation
pages.description: Consumer prices in the euro area: headline, core, services and the ECB's underlying measures.

sections.title: Headline and core
sections.intro: Headline inflation is what you pay at the till. Core strips out energy and food, which swing the most, to show the trend underneath.

sections.title: Across countries
sections.intro: The same euro, different price rises: inflation by member state over the last year.

pages.title: Financial
pages.description: Bond yields, the euro and the cost of borrowing.

sections.title: Bonds
sections.intro: Government bond yields set the floor for what mortgages and business loans cost.

sections.title: The euro
sections.intro: A stronger euro makes imports cheaper and exports harder to sell.

pages.title: ECB
pages.description: The European Central Bank's interest rates and what markets pay for overnight money.

sections.title: Policy rates
sections.intro: The deposit facility rate is the ECB's main lever. Market rates follow it within a day.

pages.title: Fiscal
pages.description: Public debt and deficits, for the euro area and its members.

sections.title: Debt
sections.intro: Government debt as a share of what the economy produces in a year.

sections.title: Deficits
sections.intro: The gap between what governments spend and what they collect.

pages.title: International
pages.description: The euro area's trade and money flows with the rest of the world.

sections.title: Current account
sections.intro: A surplus means the euro area earns more from the world than it spends there.

pages.title: Europe
pages.description: Indicators only Europe has: surveys, energy and the gaps between member states.

sections.title: Surveys
sections.intro: The European Commission asks businesses and households every month how things are going.

sections.title: Energy
sections.intro: Gas storage and wholesale power prices.
